title: Format a Report Line
oneLiner: Build one fixed-width line of a report: a left-aligned name, a right-aligned quantity, and two money columns with two decimals.
keyTakeaway: Format strings line columns up for you: {value,width:format} in C#, {value:>width.decimals} in Python. A negative C# width (or < in Python) left-aligns; F2 (or .2f) gives two decimals; N2 (or ,.2f) adds thousands separators too.
explanation:
Write FormatRow(name, qty, price) returning one line of a parts report, four columns separated by |: the name left-aligned in 10 characters, the quantity right-aligned in 5, the unit price right-aligned in 10 with exactly 2 decimal places, and the line total (qty × price) right-aligned in 12 with 2 decimals and a comma between thousands. FormatRow("Pump", 3, 1249.5) gives "Pump␣␣␣␣␣␣|␣␣␣␣3|␣␣␣1249.50|␣␣␣␣3,748.50". Names are at most 10 characters.

In C#, one interpolated string does it: $"{name,-10}|{qty,5}|{price,10:F2}|{qty * price,12:N2}". F2 is fixed-point with 2 decimals, N2 adds thousands separators. In Python: f"{name:<10}|{qty:>5}|{price:>10.2f}|{qty * price:>12,.2f}". The comma in ,.2f asks for thousands separators.

C# formats numbers using the computer's culture, and the checker runs with the invariant culture, which writes a point for decimals and commas for thousands, matching Python. On a computer set to, say, German, the same C# code would print 1.249,50; for text other programs read, pass CultureInfo.InvariantCulture to ToString.

visualizationSteps.message: The name, left-aligned in 10 characters: padded with spaces on the right.
The quantity, right-aligned in 5: padded on the left.
The price with exactly 2 decimals (F2), right-aligned in 10.
The total, 3 × 1249.5 = 3748.5, with a thousands separator and 2 decimals (N2), right-aligned in 12.
Joined with | between the columns. ␣ marks each padding space; the brackets only show where each column starts and ends.

complexity.note: A fixed number of fields formatted to fixed widths; the line is always about 40 characters.

referenceSolutions.python:
def format_row(name, qty, price):
    return f"{name:<10}|{qty:>5}|{price:>10.2f}|{qty * price:>12,.2f}"
